name: Clue-gated whodunit
summary: A branching mystery where you only have time to visit some places, each visit can add a clue, and the accusation at the end only lands if you gathered enough clues on the right suspect.
core_loop: read a short scene → pick one of up to three choices → maybe gain a clue or trust → choose which place to search next → accuse at the finale
rules: only a limited number of locations can be visited before the deadline
choices add clues or change a trust meter, and some unlock later options
an accusation needs a clue threshold to win; a wrong or thin accusation is a bad ending
a hidden best ending needs a specific path and stat
win: accuse the right suspect with enough clues, or reach the secret ending
lose: a bad ending: wrong suspect, too few clues, or a reckless choice
scoring: clues × 100 + trust × 50 + ending bonus
social_hooks: compare which ending you reached with friends
challenge a friend to find the secret ending
example_prompts: a spooky wizard school mystery where my roommate gets framed for stealing something and I have to find the real thief before dawn
a detective game where I question suspects and name the killer
a sherlock style mystery with clues and a wrong accusation ending

name: Meter trade-off adventure
summary: A branching adventure where every choice trades two meters against each other (loyalty against heat, say), and the meters decide which route works at the climax.
core_loop: read a scene → pick a choice that moves two meters → meters gate later routes → reach an ending at the climax
rules: each choice raises one meter and often costs the other
a climax choice succeeds only if a meter is under or over a threshold
one character gives deliberately bad advice
a secret ending needs a specific earlier choice
win: reach a good ending with the meters in range
lose: a bad ending from a trap route or a meter out of range
scoring: meter values × points + ending bonus
example_prompts: a space opera adventure where I'm a smuggler pulled into a rebellion against an evil empire, with a big escape at the end and maybe a traitor
a star wars style story where I choose between my crew and getting away clean
a pirate adventure with choices where reputation and danger change the ending

name: Bait the leaker
summary: A branching social drama where you tell different people different fake secrets, see which one leaks, and use that to unmask the anonymous source while keeping your reputation up.
core_loop: read a scene → choose who to tell which secret → watch what leaks → collect proof → unmask the source at the finale
rules: a planted fake secret that leaks proves who heard it
tipping off the suspect closes the trap
unmasking needs enough clues and a reputation above a floor
win: unmask the right person with enough clues and reputation, or find the secret truce ending
lose: a bad ending from accusing the wrong person, thin proof or low reputation
scoring: clues × 100 + reputation × 50 + ending bonus
social_hooks: dare a friend to find who leaked faster
example_prompts: a messy rich-kid prep school drama where an anonymous gossip account is leaking everyone's secrets and I have to figure out who runs it
a gossip girl game where I trap the anonymous blogger
an office drama where someone leaks emails and I set a trap to find them

name: Heist crew story
summary: A branching heist where you pick a small crew from a few specialists, each opening a different route, then run the job while an alarm meter climbs; one crew member may betray you.
core_loop: pick crew → choose a plan and route their skills open → make choices that raise or lower the alarm → escape or get caught
rules: each crew member unlocks one route or trick
risky choices raise the alarm; casing and rehearsal lower it
one crew member can double-cross you unless you plan for it
the escape fails if the alarm is too high
win: get away clean, or pull the secret long con
scoring: (alarm cap − alarm) × 100 + ending bonus
example_prompts: a heist story game where I pick my crew and plan how to steal back a priceless egg from a crooked collector's masked party, and someone might double-cross me
an ocean's eleven style game where I plan a casino robbery
a money heist story where I choose my team and someone betrays us

name: Orbit timing tap
summary: A marker circles a ring; tap when it passes through a target zone, with a smaller perfect slice in the middle. Streaks multiply points, and the zone jumps after each hit.
core_loop: watch the marker orbit → tap as it crosses the zone → score clean or perfect × combo → zone moves → repeat until time runs out
rules: a tap inside the zone scores; inside the perfect slice scores more
points are multiplied by the combo
an early tap costs points, breaks the combo and briefly stuns
letting the marker pass the zone costs a life
lose: run out of lives from missed zones
scoring: perfect or clean points × combo; rank titles by total
example_prompts: a stupid brainrot game where you farm aura by tapping on beat
a tap on the beat game where streaks multiply your score
a sigma timing game where you hit the perfect zone

name: Two-way speed sort
summary: Cards flash up one at a time and you call each one of two categories as fast as you can; one draining bar is the clock, right calls refill it and wrong calls drain it.
core_loop: read a card → tap or swipe one of two answers → right refills the bar, wrong drains it → bar drains faster over time
rules: right calls add time and score with a speed bonus
wrong calls take time off
the drain speeds up over the run
a streak multiplies points
scoring: points per right call + speed bonus, × streak multiplier
example_prompts: npc or main character game where weird situations pop up and you have to sort them super fast
a swipe left or right game sorting red flags and green flags fast
is it a hotdog or not speed sorting game

name: Dodge and collect waves
aliases: catch the good avoid the bad
summary: Drag a character around the screen to grab pickups while hazards stream in from two edges in waves; a streak of pickups triggers a short power mode where hazards become food.
core_loop: drag to steer → grab pickups → dodge hazards from the top and side → build a streak → power mode → clear the wave
rules: touching a hazard costs a life, clears nearby hazards and gives grace
a streak of pickups without a hit triggers power mode
in power mode hazards are harmless and worth points
clearing all waves wins
scoring: points per pickup, doubled in power mode, plus points per hazard eaten
example_prompts: goblin mode game where you grab snacks at 2am and dodge responsibilities
a game where I catch falling candy and dodge vegetables
grab coins and avoid bombs coming from everywhere

name: Judged reply quiz
summary: Someone says a line and you pick the best of four replies before a short timer runs out; a panel of judges reacts with score cards, and the multiplier heats up every few rounds.
core_loop: read the line → pick one of four replies fast → judges react and score → heat rises every few rounds
rules: one reply per line is the smooth one
answering faster adds a speed bonus
wrong picks or timeouts cost a heart
the multiplier steps up every few rounds
lose: lose all hearts or run out the clock
scoring: points per right reply + speed bonus and streak, × heat; a title by total
content_needs: one right and three wrong replies each
difficulty_levers: how close the wrong replies are
example_prompts: rizz or flop quiz where you pick the least cringe thing to say and judges react
a love island game where I choose the smoothest pickup line
pick the right thing to say to your boss before time runs out

name: Lane dodge race
summary: Tap left or right to swerve one lane at a time across several lanes, dodging falling hazards and grabbing pickups until the finish; passing a hazard in the next lane scores a near miss.
core_loop: tap a side to change lane → dodge hazards → grab pickups for a streak → skim near misses for bonus → reach the finish
rules: a hit costs a life, resets the streak and gives grace
a hazard passing in the adjacent lane is a near miss bonus
pickups score more with a longer streak
hazards speed up over the race
scoring: pickups × streak plus near-miss bonuses
example_prompts: a broom racing game at a magic school where I dodge storm clouds and grab sparks
a quidditch flying race dodging bludgers
a highway game where I switch lanes to avoid cars

name: Narrowing canyon shooter
summary: Drag an auto-firing ship side to side down a canyon that narrows each wave, shooting enemies and dodging their shots, ending with a boss that has a health bar.
core_loop: drag to aim → auto-fire hits enemies → dodge shots and walls → clear the wave → canyon narrows → boss wave
rules: the ship fires on its own
walls close in each wave and hurt on contact
a chain of kills multiplies points and resets on a hit
the last wave is a boss with HP and volleys
scoring: points per kill × chain, per hit on the boss, plus a bonus for lives left
example_prompts: a space fighter flying down a narrow canyon shooting drones, with a big boss target at the end
an x-wing trench run where I blast tie fighters and hit the exhaust port
a space invaders style game with a boss at the end

name: Endless gap jumper
summary: The runner moves on its own; tap to jump and tap again to double-jump over obstacles and gaps, while pickups float along the ideal jump arc.
core_loop: run automatically → tap to jump obstacles and gaps → double-jump to recover → grab pickups on the arc → go as far as you can
rules: tap to jump, tap in the air to double-jump
hitting an obstacle or falling into a gap costs a life
pickups trace the ideal jump line
speed rises over distance
scoring: pickups × combo plus points per distance
example_prompts: an endless runner where I jump across city rooftops at night collecting letters
a spider-man rooftop runner
a mario style endless jump game

name: Slice-drop stacker
summary: A layer slides back and forth above the stack; tap to drop it, and whatever overhangs the layer below is sliced off, so the stack narrows unless you drop perfectly.
core_loop: watch the layer slide → tap to drop → overhang is sliced off → perfect drops grow it back → next layer
rules: the part that overhangs is cut away
a near-perfect drop restores some width
a drop that misses entirely costs a life
reaching the target height wins
lose: miss the stack too many times
scoring: points per layer + combo bonus for perfect drops
example_prompts: a cozy one-more-try game where you stack cake layers as high as you can
a stack the blocks game where misaligned parts get cut off
build the tallest pancake tower by timing each drop

name: Weighted personality quiz
summary: A short quiz with no right answers: each pick adds weighted points to one or two outcomes, a timer rewards answering on instinct, and the result card reveals which outcome you are.
core_loop: read a question → tap an answer before the timer → points go to outcomes → after the last question reveal your outcome card
rules: each answer adds points to one outcome and fewer to another
faster answers score conviction
too many timeouts end the quiz
a near tie between the top two outcomes gives a torn result
win: finish with a clear top outcome
lose: time out too often, or end in a tie
scoring: conviction points per answer plus the winning margin
social_hooks: post your result in the group chat
see which outcome each friend got
example_prompts: a which-house-are-you quiz for my friends with a magic school vibe, so we can all post our results in the chat
which avenger are you quiz
a which pokemon type are you quiz to share with friends

name: Who said it
summary: Read a line or post and pick which of several characters wrote it, using each character's distinctive voice as the clue, racing a friend's score.
core_loop: read a post → pick the author from four suspects before the timer → streak grows → pass the friend's score
rules: each character has a recognisable voice
a wrong pick or timeout costs a life
right picks score more with a streak
passing the friend's score wins
lose: lose all lives, run out of posts, or hit the time limit
scoring: base + streak bonus per right pick
social_hooks: quotes from people in a Group
example_prompts: a gossip trivia game at a fancy prep school where you guess who wrote each anonymous post, so I can challenge my roommate to beat my score
guess which friends character said the quote
who tweeted it: guess the celebrity from the post

name: Letter cryptogram
summary: A short message is shown in a substitution cipher; guess letters on a keyboard, and each right letter decodes every copy of it in the message. A few wrong guesses per message are allowed.
core_loop: study the coded words → guess a letter → every copy decodes → use word shapes to guess more → crack the message → next message
rules: every letter maps to another letter, none to itself
a right letter scores per copy it reveals
wrong letters cost a life, refilled per message
everyone gets the same messages each day
lose: too many wrong letters in one message, or the clock runs out
scoring: points per revealed copy plus a bonus for lives left
social_hooks: the whole group chat gets the same daily messages
example_prompts: a daily space puzzle for our group chat, like decoding a secret message from a rebel ship
a daily cryptogram for our group
decode a secret harry potter message one letter at a time

name: Pass-and-play stacker
summary: Friends take turns on one phone dropping a swinging piece onto a shared tower; every piece keeps its builder's colour, wobbly drops narrow the tower for the next person, and three tumbles end it.
core_loop: watch the piece swing → tap to drop → score by how centred it is → pass the phone → next builder
rules: players alternate turns behind a pass-the-phone screen
a piece whose middle misses the one below tumbles
off-centre drops narrow the next piece; perfect drops widen it
three tumbles end the game for everyone
win: finish every turn without three tumbles
scoring: up to 10 per drop by centredness, perfect bonus, team total plus each player's own
social_hooks: a sleepover or party on one phone
everyone sees whose pieces held the tower
example_prompts: a pass-the-phone party game for a sleepover where we all build something together
a pass the phone tower building game for a party
take turns stacking blocks without knocking the tower down

name: Next-line story quiz
summary: A short scripted scene (a press conference, an interview, a cooking show) cut into beats. At each beat you guess the next line from three; the reveal shows the real line, which is always the funniest, and what happened next.
core_loop: read the quote card → guess the next line → reveal the real line and the punchline → next beat → end card: how many you called
rules: beats play in order, never shuffled
the real line is the joke, the twist or the disaster, and the other guesses are plausible but tame
no lives and no timer: nothing is lost
each beat escalates the scene
win: reach the end of the clip
scoring: unranked: lines called out of the beats; friends compare how often they picked the same lines
social_hooks: see how in sync you were with a friend
share the line that got you
content_needs: 8 beats: speaker, setup line, ask, the real line, two tame guesses, the punchline
difficulty_levers: how plausible the tame guesses are
example_prompts: a press conference where the mayor’s new bridge goes really badly, as a quiz where you guess what he says
a funny clip of a politician interview going wrong broken into kahoot questions
a job interview gone wrong where you guess the candidate’s next answer
notes: mechanic of gold game gold_the_podium. Real people only as labelled parody (tag PARODY) with cartoon art; never write a quote that reads as real reporting.

name: Narrator-voice story quiz
summary: A character narrates a film (a cat hosting a nature documentary, a toddler on a cooking show) and keeps going off script. Once you learn their voice you can guess their next line; the reveal shows what they really said.
core_loop: read the narration → guess the narrator’s next line → reveal → learn the voice → next scene
rules: the narrator’s logic is consistent, so later beats are guessable
some beats have a picture, some are text only
nothing is lost
scoring: unranked: lines called; friends compare picks
content_needs: 8 beats in one consistent comic voice
example_prompts: a nature documentary narrated by a cat who keeps getting distracted
a cooking show hosted by a toddler where you guess what he says next
a sports commentator who only cares about the snacks

name: Which came first (pairs)
summary: Two events from different worlds (a university and an empire, a gadget and an invention); tap the one that happened first. The reveal gives both dates. Pairs are picked so intuition misleads and you reason from anchors.
core_loop: read two events → tap the earlier one → see both dates and the gap → streak or lose a life
pieces: question card that turns into the dates
rules: each pair crosses domains so no single date answers it
the reveal shows both years
a wrong call costs a life; a streak adds a bonus
scoring: 100 per right call + streak bonus
social_hooks: same pairs for the group, compare scores
content_needs: pairs with verified dates and a one-line note
example_prompts: a which came first history game
guess which happened earlier, nintendo or the model t
a timeline quiz with surprising pairs
notes: mechanic of gold game gold_first_things_first. Shows the notes in the question card while locked (quiz reveal_ms).

name: Mate in one (pick the move)
summary: A chess position drawn as a picture and four candidate moves in notation; exactly one is checkmate. Every wrong move is a plausible check that fails for a concrete reason, so you must calculate escape squares.
core_loop: study the board → pick one of four moves → reveal why it mates or fails → next position
rules: one candidate mates; the others check or threaten but fail
positions are verified with a chess engine before shipping
a wrong move costs a life
scoring: 100 per mate
content_needs: positions (FEN) checked by a move generator
example_prompts: mate in one chess puzzles
a chess tactics quiz for my chess club
find the checkmate
notes: mechanic of gold game gold_one_move. The board is a sprite with one frame per puzzle (picture, frame = get_or(order, qi, 0)); never invent a position without checking it.
